records.title: Fever
records.overview: Fever is a temporary increase in body temperature, often caused by the immune system responding to an infection such as a cold, flu, or other illness. Common symptoms can include feeling hot or chilled, sweating, tiredness, headache, and muscle aches. Fever itself is usually a sign that the body is responding to something rather than a disease on its own. Drinking enough fluids, getting adequate rest, and monitoring symptoms can help while the underlying illness improves. If a fever is very high, lasts for several days, keeps returning, or occurs with concerning symptoms such as difficulty breathing, severe headache, confusion, stiff neck, or significant dehydration, medical attention should be sought. For children and teenagers, the appropriate response can depend on age and other symptoms, so it is best to involve a parent/guardian and a healthcare professional when you're concerned
records.medicine: Consult a qualified healthcare professional for condition-specific medicine guidance.
records.suggestions: Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, persistent, or worsening.

records.title: common cold
records.overview: The common cold is a mild infection of the upper respiratory tract, usually caused by viruses. Common symptoms include a runny or blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, mild headache, and tiredness. Fever may occur but is generally mild. Most common colds improve on their own within several days to about a week. Management usually focuses on rest, adequate fluids, and relieving symptoms. Warm fluids and adequate sleep may help with comfort. Antibiotics generally do not help because the common cold is usually caused by viruses. If symptoms become severe, last unusually long, or cause breathing difficulties, a healthcare professional should be consulted
records.medicine: Symptom-relief medicines may sometimes be used under appropriate guidance; antibiotics are not normally useful for an uncomplicated viral cold
records.suggestions: Get adequate rest, drink fluids, wash hands regularly, and avoid close contact with others when sick

records.title: Influenza
records.overview: Influenza, commonly called the flu, is a contagious respiratory infection caused by influenza viruses. Symptoms can appear suddenly and may include fever, cough, sore throat, headache, muscle aches, chills, and significant tiredness. Compared with an ordinary cold, influenza can cause more intense body aches and fatigue. Treatment depends on the person's age, health status, and severity of illness. Rest and adequate fluid intake are important. In some situations, healthcare professionals may prescribe antiviral medicines, particularly for people at higher risk of complications or when treatment is started early. Medical evaluation is important if symptoms are severe
records.medicine: Antiviral treatment may be prescribed by a healthcare professional when appropriate; do not self-select medication
records.suggestions: Rest, maintain hydration, avoid spreading the infection to others, and seek medical advice if symptoms become severe

records.title: COVID-19
records.overview: COVID-19 is an infectious disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Symptoms can include fever, cough, sore throat, tiredness, headache, muscle aches, congestion, and sometimes changes in taste or smell. Symptoms vary considerably between people, and some individuals may have mild symptoms while others can become seriously ill. Management depends on the severity of the infection and the individual's risk factors. Mild illness may be managed with rest, fluids, and monitoring. People with significant breathing problems, worsening symptoms, or other concerning symptoms should receive medical attention. Healthcare professionals may recommend specific treatments for people who are at higher risk
records.medicine: Treatment varies according to severity and individual risk; prescription antiviral treatment may be considered by a healthcare professional in appropriate cases
records.suggestions: Follow current public-health guidance, maintain hygiene, stay home when unwell when appropriate, and seek medical help for serious symptoms

records.title: Tuberculosis
records.overview: Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It most commonly affects the lungs but can affect other parts of the body. Symptoms of pulmonary TB can include a persistent cough, fever, night sweating, tiredness, loss of appetite, and unexplained weight loss. TB can spread through the air when a person with infectious pulmonary TB coughs or sneezes. TB requires proper medical diagnosis and a carefully supervised treatment course. Treatment generally involves a combination of specific anti-tuberculosis medicines taken for several months. Completing the entire prescribed treatment is extremely important because stopping treatment early can contribute to drug resistance
records.medicine: TB requires a prescribed combination of antituberculosis medicines under medical supervision
records.suggestions: Anyone with a persistent cough or other concerning symptoms should receive medical evaluation. People diagnosed with TB should follow their healthcare professional's treatment plan carefully

records.title: Malaria
records.overview: Malaria is a serious infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites and transmitted through the bites of infected mosquitoes. Symptoms commonly include fever, chills, sweating, headache, tiredness, and body aches. Some forms of malaria can become severe and may cause serious complications if treatment is delayed. Treatment depends on the malaria species, geographical location, severity of infection, and other factors. Healthcare professionals use specific antimalarial medicines based on these factors. Malaria should not be treated by choosing a medicine independently because the appropriate treatment can vary
records.medicine: Antimalarial treatment is selected by a healthcare professional according to the type and severity of malaria
records.suggestions: Seek medical testing when malaria is suspected, use mosquito-bite prevention measures, and obtain prompt medical care for persistent or severe fever

records.title: Dengue
records.overview: Dengue is a viral infection transmitted mainly by infected Aedes mosquitoes. It can cause sudden fever, headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain, nausea, and sometimes a skin rash. Most people recover with appropriate supportive care, but some cases can become severe. There is no routine antibiotic treatment for dengue because it is caused by a virus. Management generally involves adequate fluids, rest, and medical monitoring. Some medicines can increase bleeding risk, so people with suspected dengue should not choose pain or fever medicines on their own without medical advice
records.medicine: Supportive treatment and fluid management are commonly used; medication choices should be determined by a healthcare professional
records.suggestions: Stay hydrated, rest, get appropriate testing when dengue is suspected, and seek urgent medical attention if symptoms worsen or unusual bleeding, severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, or other warning signs occur

records.title: Typhoid fever
records.overview: Typhoid fever is an infection caused by Salmonella Typhi. It is commonly spread through contaminated food or water. Symptoms can include prolonged fever, headache, weakness, abdominal discomfort, diarrhea or constipation, and loss of appetite. Without appropriate treatment, the infection can become serious. Typhoid generally requires antibiotics prescribed after appropriate medical evaluation. The choice of antibiotic depends on local antibiotic resistance patterns and the individual's circumstances. Completing the prescribed course is important when treatment is given

records.suggestions: Drink safe water, maintain good hand hygiene, consume properly prepared food, and seek medical evaluation for persistent fever

records.title: Cholera
records.overview: Cholera is an intestinal infection caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae. It can cause sudden, severe watery diarrhea and vomiting, which can lead to dangerous dehydration. Severe dehydration can develop quickly, making prompt treatment particularly important. The most important part of cholera management is rapid replacement of lost fluids and electrolytes. In severe cases, treatment may require intravenous fluids and antibiotics may be prescribed by healthcare professionals. Prevention depends heavily on safe drinking water, sanitation, and good hygiene

records.title: Measles
records.overview: Measles is a highly contagious viral infection. It commonly begins with fever, cough, runny nose, and red or watery eyes, followed by a characteristic skin rash. The infection can sometimes cause serious complications, particularly in vulnerable individuals. There is no routine antibiotic treatment for uncomplicated measles because it is caused by a virus. Treatment generally focuses on supportive care, hydration, rest, and monitoring for complications. Vaccination is the most important method of preventing measles
records.medicine: Supportive care is generally used; healthcare professionals may provide additional treatment depending on complications and individual circumstances
records.suggestions: Follow recommended vaccination schedules, avoid exposing others when infected, and seek medical attention if symptoms become severe

records.title: Chickenpox
records.overview: Chickenpox is a contagious viral infection caused by the varicella-zoster virus. It commonly produces an itchy rash that develops into fluid-filled spots and later crusts over. Fever, tiredness, and loss of appetite can also occur. Most healthy children recover without serious complications, although complications can occur. Treatment generally focuses on relieving symptoms and preventing complications. Keeping the skin clean and avoiding scratching can help reduce the risk of secondary infection. In certain situations, healthcare professionals may prescribe antiviral treatment, especially for people at increased risk of complications

records.title: Hepatitis
records.overview: Hepatitis means inflammation of the liver and can have several causes, including viruses such as hepatitis A, B, and C. Symptoms may include tiredness, nausea, abdominal discomfort, fever, dark urine, pale stools, and yellowing of the skin or eyes. Some types can become chronic and cause long-term liver problems. Treatment depends strongly on the type and cause of hepatitis. Some forms mainly require supportive care, while chronic hepatitis B or hepatitis C may require specific antiviral treatment under specialist medical supervision. Because different types of hepatitis have different treatments, proper testing is important before treatment is selected
records.medicine: Treatment varies according to the specific type of hepatitis; antiviral therapy may be prescribed for certain forms
records.suggestions: Seek appropriate testing, avoid sharing personal items that may carry blood, maintain good hygiene, and follow medical advice

records.title: Pneumonia
records.overview: Pneumonia is an infection or inflammation of the lungs that can be caused by bacteria, viruses, fungi, or other organisms. Symptoms may include cough, fever, chills, chest discomfort, tiredness, and difficulty breathing. The severity can range from mild to lifethreatening, particularly in vulnerable individuals. Treatment depends on the cause and severity. Bacterial pneumonia may require antibiotics prescribed by a healthcare professional, while viral pneumonia may require supportive care or specific antiviral treatment in selected circumstances. Severe pneumonia may require oxygen or hospital-based treatment

records.title: Hypertension
records.overview: Hypertension is a condition in which blood pressure remains higher than the recommended range over time. It often does not cause noticeable symptoms, which is why it is sometimes called a “silent” condition. When blood pressure remains uncontrolled for a long period, it can increase the risk of problems affecting the heart, brain, kidneys, and blood vessels. Treatment usually involves lifestyle changes and, when needed, medicines prescribed by a healthcare professional. Regular blood-pressure monitoring, reducing excessive salt intake, maintaining healthy activity, getting adequate sleep, and following the prescribed treatment plan can help control blood pressure
records.medicine: Blood-pressure-lowering medicines may be prescribed depending on the individual's blood pressure and health history
records.suggestions: Monitor blood pressure regularly and follow medical advice. Seek medical attention for extremely high readings accompanied by symptoms such as severe headache, chest pain, confusion, or difficulty breathing

records.title: Coronary artery disease
records.overview: Coronary artery disease occurs when the blood vessels supplying the heart become narrowed or blocked, commonly because of the buildup of fatty deposits. It can reduce blood flow to the heart muscle and may cause chest discomfort, shortness of breath, tiredness, or symptoms during physical activity. Treatment depends on the severity of the disease and may include lifestyle changes, prescribed medicines, and sometimes medical procedures. Controlling blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, and other risk factors is important. Regular medical follow-up can help reduce the risk of complications
records.medicine: Healthcare professionals may prescribe medicines to control cholesterol, blood pressure, blood clotting, or heart-related symptoms depending on the individual
records.suggestions: Seek urgent medical care for new or severe chest pain, especially when accompanied by breathing difficulty, sweating, faintness, or pain spreading to the arm or jaw

records.title: Heart failure
records.overview: Heart failure occurs when the heart cannot pump blood effectively enough to meet the body's needs. It can cause symptoms such as shortness of breath, tiredness, swelling of the legs or ankles, and difficulty breathing when lying down. Heart failure can develop because of conditions such as coronary artery disease, high blood pressure, or damage to the heart muscle. Treatment is individualized and may include lifestyle changes, monitoring, prescribed medicines, and sometimes devices or procedures. Managing the underlying cause is an important part of treatment. Regular follow-up helps healthcare professionals monitor the condition and adjust treatment
records.medicine: Several types of heart medicines may be prescribed depending on the type and severity of heart failure
records.suggestions: Follow the prescribed treatment plan and monitor symptoms. Sudden severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, or fainting requires urgent medical attention

records.title: Anemia
records.overview: Anemia occurs when the blood does not have enough healthy red blood cells or hemoglobin to carry oxygen effectively. It can cause tiredness, weakness, dizziness, headaches, and shortness of breath, depending on its severity. Iron deficiency is one common cause, but anemia can also result from vitamin deficiencies, chronic diseases, blood loss, or inherited conditions. Treatment depends on the underlying cause. Some people may need nutritional changes or supplements, while others require treatment for an underlying disease. It is important to determine the cause rather than taking supplements without appropriate evaluation
records.medicine: Iron or vitamin supplements may be recommended when a deficiency is confirmed, while other types of anemia require different treatment
records.suggestions: Eat a varied, nutritious diet and seek medical evaluation for persistent tiredness, weakness, or unexplained symptoms

records.title: Sickle cell disease
records.overview: Sickle cell disease is an inherited blood disorder in which red blood cells can become abnormally shaped. These cells can interfere with normal blood flow and may cause episodes of pain, anemia, tiredness, and increased susceptibility to certain complications. It is a lifelong condition that requires ongoing medical care. Management focuses on preventing complications, treating symptoms, maintaining adequate hydration, and monitoring overall health. Some people may receive specialized medicines or other treatments depending on their condition. Regular followup with a healthcare team is important

records.title: Leukemia
records.overview: Leukemia is a type of cancer affecting blood-forming tissues, particularly the bone marrow. It leads to the production of abnormal blood cells and can cause symptoms such as tiredness, frequent infections, easy bruising, fever, or unexplained bleeding. There are several types of leukemia, and they can behave differently. Treatment depends on the specific type and may include chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, radiation in selected situations, or stem-cell transplantation. Treatment should always be managed by a specialist oncology team

Inhaled medicines are commonly used to control airway inflammation and relieve symptoms. Identifying and avoiding personal triggers can also help reduce episodes

Common symptoms include long-lasting cough, mucus production, wheezing, tiredness, and shortness of breath. Treatment focuses on reducing symptoms, improving lung function, preventing flareups, and maintaining activity. Inhaled medicines, pulmonary rehabilitation, vaccinations, and oxygen therapy in selected cases may be part of treatment

It is not contagious and can affect people of any age. Treatment is individualized and may include topical medicines, light-based therapy, or other specialist treatments. Some people choose no medical treatment and instead focus on skin protection and cosmetic approaches

records.suggestions: Protect depigmented areas from excessive sunlight and seek dermatological evaluation if new patches appear

records.title: Ringworm
records.overview: Ringworm is a fungal infection of the skin and is not caused by a worm. It can cause circular, itchy, scaly patches and can occur on different parts of the body. It can spread through direct contact with infected people, animals, or contaminated objects. Treatment usually involves appropriate antifungal treatment. The exact treatment depends on the location and severity of the infection. Keeping the affected area clean and dry can help reduce spread
records.medicine: Antifungal treatments may be used, with the appropriate type depending on the location and severity
records.suggestions: Avoid sharing towels or clothing, maintain good hygiene, and seek medical advice if the infection spreads or does not improve

records.title: Scabies
records.overview: Scabies is a contagious skin infestation caused by microscopic mites that burrow into the skin. It commonly causes intense itching, particularly at night, along with small bumps or a rash. It spreads mainly through prolonged close skin-to-skin contact. Treatment requires a specific anti-parasitic medicine prescribed or recommended by a healthcare professional. Close contacts may also need evaluation and treatment to prevent reinfection. Clothing, bedding, and towels should be handled according to medical/public-health guidance
records.medicine: Prescription or recommended anti-parasitic skin treatment is generally required; treatment should be followed exactly as directed
records.suggestions: Seek medical evaluation, avoid close contact until appropriate treatment has been completed, and follow guidance for treating household contacts and belongings

records.title: Tooth decay
records.overview: Tooth decay, also called dental caries or cavities, occurs when bacteria in the mouth produce acids that gradually damage the tooth's outer layers. It can cause sensitivity to hot or cold foods, pain, visible spots or holes in the tooth, and sometimes difficulty chewing. If untreated, decay can progress deeper into the tooth and affect the dental pulp. Treatment depends on how advanced the decay is. Early damage may sometimes be managed with fluoride treatment and improved oral hygiene, while established cavities may require a filling. If the decay reaches the inner part of the tooth, a dentist may recommend root-canal treatment or another dental procedure
records.medicine: Fluoride products may help prevent or manage early tooth decay. Pain-relief medicines may sometimes be used for discomfort, but they do not remove the underlying decay
records.suggestions: Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste, clean between the teeth, limit frequent sugary foods and drinks, and visit a dentist regularly

records.title: Toothache
records.overview: Toothache is pain or discomfort in or around a tooth. It can be caused by tooth decay, a cracked tooth, gum disease, dental infection, or problems involving the tooth's inner tissues. The pain may be constant or may become worse when eating, drinking, or applying pressure. Treatment depends on the underlying cause. A dentist needs to examine the tooth to determine whether treatment such as a filling, cleaning, root-canal treatment, or another procedure is necessary. Pain-relief treatment may temporarily reduce discomfort but does not fix the dental problem
records.medicine: Appropriate pain-relief medicine may sometimes be recommended by a healthcare professional, depending on age and health conditions. Antibiotics are not routinely needed for ordinary toothache and should only be used when a dentist or doctor determines that there is an appropriate bacterial infection
records.suggestions: Arrange a dental examination if toothache persists. Seek urgent dental/medical care if pain occurs with facial swelling, fever, difficulty swallowing, or difficulty breathing

records.title: Gingivitis
records.overview: Gingivitis is inflammation of the gums, usually caused by the buildup of plaque around the teeth. Common signs include red or swollen gums, tenderness, and bleeding during brushing or flossing. Gingivitis is an early form of gum disease and can often be improved when plaque is properly controlled. Treatment mainly involves improving oral hygiene and removing plaque and tartar. A dental professional may perform a professional cleaning if necessary. If gingivitis is not managed, it can progress to more serious gum disease that may damage the tissues supporting the teeth
records.medicine: Treatment primarily involves oral hygiene and professional dental cleaning. Specific mouth rinses or other treatments may be recommended by a dental professional when appropriate
records.suggestions: Brush gently twice a day with fluoride toothpaste, clean between teeth daily, avoid tobacco exposure, and attend regular dental checkups

records.title: Mouth ulcers
records.overview: Mouth ulcers are small sores that can develop inside the mouth, including on the tongue, cheeks, lips, or gums. They may cause pain or burning, particularly while eating spicy, acidic, or salty foods. Minor ulcers can occur after accidental biting, irritation, stress, or other causes and often heal on their own. Treatment generally focuses on reducing irritation and managing discomfort while the ulcer heals. Avoiding foods that make the ulcer painful and maintaining good oral hygiene can help. Persistent, unusually large, frequently recurring, or unexplained ulcers should be evaluated by a healthcare professional or dentist
records.medicine: Protective or pain-relieving oral treatments may sometimes be recommended by a healthcare professional depending on the cause and severity
records.suggestions: Avoid irritating foods, maintain gentle oral hygiene, drink adequate fluids, and seek professional evaluation if an ulcer does not heal or keeps returning

records.title: Dental abscess
records.overview: A dental abscess is a collection of infected material that develops because of a bacterial infection around a tooth or gum. It can cause severe tooth pain, swelling, sensitivity, fever, and sometimes an unpleasant taste in the mouth. The infection can spread to surrounding tissues if it is not treated. A dental abscess requires professional dental treatment rather than simply treating the pain. Depending on the location and severity, a dentist may drain the infection, perform root-canal treatment, or remove the affected tooth. Antibiotics may sometimes be prescribed when there are signs of spreading infection or systemic illness
records.medicine: Antibiotics are used only when medically indicated and should be prescribed by a dentist or doctor. Pain-relief treatment may help with symptoms but does not eliminate the abscess
records.suggestions: Seek dental care promptly. Facial or neck swelling with difficulty breathing or swallowing is an emergency and requires immediate medical attention

records.title: Acidity
records.overview: Acidity commonly refers to symptoms caused by stomach acid irritating the upper digestive tract. It may cause a burning sensation in the upper abdomen or chest, sour taste in the mouth, belching, or discomfort after eating. Symptoms can sometimes become worse after large meals or when lying down soon after eating. Management usually involves eating regular balanced meals, avoiding foods that personally trigger symptoms, and not lying down immediately after eating. If acidity occurs frequently or is severe, a healthcare professional should evaluate the cause because conditions such as GERD or gastritis may be involved
records.medicine: Healthcare professionals may recommend acid-reducing or acid-neutralizing medicines depending on the cause and frequency of symptoms
records.suggestions: Eat slowly, avoid very large meals, stay upright after eating, and seek medical advice if symptoms are frequent or persistent

records.title: Indigestion
records.overview: Indigestion, also called dyspepsia, refers to discomfort in the upper part of the digestive system. It can cause fullness, bloating, belching, nausea, or a burning sensation after eating. It may occur occasionally after eating too quickly, eating a large meal, or consuming foods that trigger symptoms. Treatment depends on the underlying cause. Simple cases may improve with changes in eating habits and avoiding individual triggers. Persistent indigestion can sometimes be associated with gastritis, ulcers, GERD, or other digestive conditions and may require medical evaluation
records.medicine: Depending on the cause, a healthcare professional may recommend medicines that reduce stomach acid or relieve digestive symptoms
records.suggestions: Eat slowly, avoid overeating, keep track of foods that trigger symptoms, and consult a healthcare professional if indigestion repeatedly occurs

records.title: Constipation
records.overview: Constipation occurs when bowel movements become less frequent or difficult to pass, or when stools become hard and dry. It can cause abdominal discomfort, bloating, and a feeling that the bowel has not completely emptied. Common contributing factors include inadequate dietary fiber, insufficient fluid intake, reduced physical activity, and changes in routine. Management often involves increasing fiber gradually, drinking adequate fluids, and maintaining regular physical activity. Some people may need short-term treatment recommended by a healthcare professional. Persistent constipation should be evaluated to identify an underlying cause
records.medicine: Fiber supplements or certain laxatives may sometimes be recommended, but they should be used appropriately and according to professional guidance
records.suggestions: Include fiber-rich foods, drink adequate fluids, stay physically active, and seek medical advice if constipation persists or occurs with significant abdominal pain or bleeding. Diarrhea involves frequent passage of loose or watery stools. It can result from infections, contaminated food or water, certain medicines, food intolerance, or digestive conditions. It may be accompanied by abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, or fever. The main concern with significant diarrhea is dehydration because the body loses fluids and electrolytes. Drinking appropriate fluids and replacing electrolytes can help. Treatment depends on the cause, and some cases require medical evaluation, particularly when diarrhea is severe or persistent. Medicine information: Treatment depends on the cause. Some symptom-relief medicines may be appropriate in certain situations, while others should be avoided when specific symptoms or infections are present. Suggestions: Maintain hydration, practice good hand hygiene, and seek medical care for severe dehydration, persistent diarrhea, blood in the stool, or significant illness. Gastroenteritis is inflammation of the stomach and intestines, commonly caused by viral or bacterial infections. It can produce diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, nausea, and sometimes fever. It can spread through contaminated food, water, or contact with infected people. Treatment mainly focuses on replacing fluids and electrolytes and allowing the digestive system to recover. Antibiotics are not routinely useful for viral gastroenteritis and are only appropriate for certain bacterial infections when prescribed by a healthcare professional. Medicine information: Treatment depends on the cause; fluid and electrolyte replacement is particularly important. Suggestions: Drink adequate fluids, wash hands thoroughly, prepare food safely, and seek medical attention if there is severe dehydration, persistent vomiting, blood in the stool, or worsening symptoms. Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining. It can cause upper abdominal pain or discomfort, nausea, vomiting, bloating, and indigestion. Causes can include Helicobacter pylori infection, certain medicines, alcohol exposure, or other conditions. Treatment depends on the underlying cause. Healthcare professionals may recommend acid-reducing treatment or treatment for an underlying infection when appropriate. Identifying and managing the cause is important because untreated gastritis can sometimes lead to complications. Medicine information: Acid-reducing medicines or other treatments may be recommended depending on the cause. If H. pylori infection is confirmed, specific prescription treatment may be required. Suggestions: Avoid known stomach irritants, follow professional advice, and seek medical evaluation for persistent symptoms or signs of gastrointestinal bleeding
